business_problem: EY wanted enterprise-scale generative AI that employees could use in a private, secure environment, but off-the-shelf tools lacked EY-specific context and raised data privacy, information security, governance and executive alignment concerns that could stall adoption.
solution_summary: EY chose to build EY.ai EYQ as a custom generative AI ecosystem instead of buying consumer-grade tools. The platform was developed in quick phases and is powered by EY Fabric, whose reusable cloud, data, intelligence, development and experience components gave teams a scalable foundation. EYQ began with a secure ChatGPT-like experience, then expanded into domain-specific conversational agents that answer questions in areas such as HR and client delivery using EY knowledge and data. A robust orchestration framework decides which agents, or which combination of agents, should respond based on user context, while prompt management lets users improve and share prompts through a centralized library. Shared workspaces make EYQ a multiuser collaborator, and developer environments let technologists publish new copilots from Microsoft Copilot Studio into the ecosystem. Microsoft Azure and Azure OpenAI service provide the core infrastructure for one of EY's largest private GenAI environments.

data_flow: EY knowledge, data and domain context are routed through EY Fabric into EYQ's private Azure and Azure OpenAI environment. The orchestration framework selects the relevant conversational agents, prompt management improves user inputs, shared workspaces support team collaboration, and new copilots built in Copilot Studio can be published back into the ecosystem.
business_outcome: EY established a secure enterprise GenAI platform with broad adoption, faster internal knowledge access, shared collaboration patterns and a reusable foundation for new agents and copilots, helping the firm operate more like an AI-first organization without compromising governance or brand safety.
